title: GPU pagefault / driver handshake debug notes
content:
Notes / breadcrumbs from today's investigation. Rough, half-formed, keeping commands + outputs + hypotheses here so I don't lose context.

Symptom summary:
- Intermittent container crashes on heavy generation load. Not full host OOM; process exits with CUDA errors, sometimes OOM reported by runtime, other times NVML reports driver/library mismatch. Repro is flaky but correlates with long sequences / KV-cache growth.
- Logs show kernel pagefaults from GPU-side address ranges and then userland sees CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED or 'CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version' depending on env.

Commands tried (repro + introspection):
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
  -> GPU 0: 24576 MiB total, used spikes then resets. No persistent ECC errors.
- dmesg | grep -i nvidia -n --color
  -> repeated: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU page fault ..." followed by "NVRM: GPU at ...: GPU has fallen off the bus" cases.
- journalctl -k --since '2 hours ago' | grep -i "GPU has fallen"
- python repro minimal (inside container):
  import torch
  a = torch.randn(64, 1024, 1024, device='cuda') # intentionally large
  torch.cuda.synchronize()
  -> Sometimes returns CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY, sometimes process gets SIGABRT with stack trace from libcudart.
- strace -f -e open,read,write -s 4096 python repro.py
  -> sees /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0 -> but also ld.so finds /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (different versions)
- ldd $(python -c "import torch; import os; print(os.path.realpath(torch.__file__))") | grep cuda
  -> shows linkage to libcudart.so.11 and libcuda.so.1 (but path points at /usr/lib/nvidia-535/libcuda.so.1 in one case)
- ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so*; ls -l /usr/lib/nvidia-*/*libcuda*
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
  -> "NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 535.54.03 Tue Jan 20 2026"
- docker run --gpus all --rm -it --env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64 test-image bash
  -> inside container, nvidia-smi shows correct driver but python shows driver/runtime mismatch on import torch when container runtime libs differ.
- echo $LD_PRELOAD ; tried LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 to force loader -> sometimes changes error to immediate abort (bad idea).
- nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo() via pynvml sometimes returns -9 NVMLError_LibraryNotFound OR NVMLError_DriverNotLoaded depending on which libcuda is loaded first.

Observed error snippets (copied):
- RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.24 GiB (GPU 0; 23.61 GiB total capacity; 20.78 GiB already allocated; 1.30 GiB free; 21.45 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
- libnvidia-ml.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
- pynvml.NVMLError_DriverNotLoaded: NVML: Driver/library version mismatch
- cudaCheckError() failed: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED: unspecified launch failure
- dmesg: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, but then sometimes 31 or 43 - mixed Xid classes.

Hypotheses so far (ranked):
1) Mixed libcuda / libcudart across host and container. Old host driver (535/536) vs container CUDA runtime expect newer symbols -> intermittent handshake failure causing pagefaults on kernel side.
2) Kernel module mismatch after recent kernel update (modinfo shows driver built against older kernel) -> occasional GPU falling off bus.
3) Workload pattern creates huge persistent KV cache leading to fragmentation at driver/KV layer and then driver exposes page faults; but fragmentation alone shouldn't cause NVML driver mismatch messages.
4) LD_PRELOAD/LD_LIBRARY_PATH from base image or conda env causing different libcuda to be resolved at runtime vs what nvidia-smi reports.

Things I tried to rule out / findings:
- Rebooting host temporarily clears issue -> supports hypothesis of module mismatch or stale kernel-driver state.
- Running same container image on a fresh clean host with same driver versions reproduces less frequently -> suggests host state matters.
- Rebuilding module with dkms on kernel v6.4 produced fewer crashes but didn't eliminate driver mismatch errors seen from pynvml.
- Removing conda env and using system python made NVML messages more consistent (i.e., fewer "library not found"), points to environment-level library shadowing.

Quick reproduction attempt (minimal):
- Build tiny image: FROM nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime-ubuntu22.04, pip install torch-cu118, pynvml
- Run docker run --gpus all -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all --shm-size=1g test:repro python -c "import torch; import time; a=[torch.randn(1024,1024,device='cuda') for _ in range(40)]; time.sleep(10)"
- On some hosts this triggers Xid 79 within ~30s. On others it runs fine.

Next / TODOs (ordered):
- [ ] Run ldd/strace side-by-side against nvidia-container-cli + python to see which libcuda path user process loads vs nvidia-smi binary. Capture full open() call order.
- [ ] Add LD_DEBUG=libs to the failing container run and collect full loader trace. Compare hosts that reproduce vs hosts that don't.
- [ ] Create nightly job that toggles different LD_LIBRARY_PATH orders to surface fragile loader setups.
- [ ] Add a tiny C repro that calls cuInit() then queries NVML repeatedly and prints handle addresses; see if cuInit returns different pointers when mismatch occurs.
- [ ] Ask infra to pin kernel/driver pair on one repro node (exact matching package) and try to reproduce with same image.
- [ ] If pagefaults persist, capture full kernel oops + NVRM stack and open a ticket with NVIDIA with attached logs.

Notes to self / heuristics learned:
- "Driver/library version mismatch" often means user-space libs (libcuda/libnvidia-ml) don't match kernel module, not necessarily that driver was never installed.
- LD_PRELOAD / conda + system libs will silently cause different binaries to link; always check strace open() for libcuda paths.
- Xid 79 tends to be pagefaults; 31/43 are more serious (memory corruption, MMU faults). Keep Xid types in the bug report.

Open questions:
- Why do some hosts with same nominal driver package reproduce more often? (possible: different dkms rebuild timing, leftover /usr/lib/nvidia-XYZ directories, old ld.so_cache)
- Are we hitting a firmware or riser level issue (less likely but note for NVIDIA asks)?

Appendix: Useful commands (save this)
- strace python -e open,read -f -s 4096 -o strace.log repro.py
- LD_DEBUG=libs python repro.py 2>&1 | tee ld-debug.log
- readlink -f $(which nvidia-smi); readlink -f /usr/bin/ldconfig; ldconfig -p | grep libcuda
- modinfo nvidia; cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version; uname -a
- grep -i nvidia /var/log/kern.log; sudo journalctl -k -b | grep -i nvrm

Dropping raw snippets into ticket when filing with NVIDIA. Keep this file as working scratchpad.

-- Asha
